translation_en: Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us. I heard Abu Salih narrate from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet said: Allah Most High says: “I am as My servant expects Me to be, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a better gathering. If he draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm’s length; if he draws near to Me by an arm’s length, I draw near to him by a fathom. If he comes to Me walking, I come to him swiftly.”

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us; Hammad narrated to us, from Amr, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: When this verse was revealed—“Say: He is the One Able to send punishment upon you from above you” (6:65)—the Prophet said: “I seek refuge in Your Face.” Then this was revealed: “or from beneath your feet,” and the Prophet said: “I seek refuge in Your Face.” Then this was revealed: “or to confuse you in sects,” and the Prophet said: “This is easier.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Nafi, from Abdullah, who said: The Dajjal was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet, who said: “Allah is not hidden from you. Allah is not one-eyed”—and he pointed to his eye—“while the False Messiah, the Dajjal, is blind in his right eye, as though his eye were a floating grape.”

Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us; Qatadah informed us, who said: I heard Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, narrate from the Prophet, who said: “Allah did not send any prophet without his warning his people about the one-eyed liar. He is one-eyed, while your Lord is not one-eyed. Written between his eyes is ‘disbeliever.’”

Ishaq narrated to us; Affan narrated to us; Wuhayb narrated to us; Musa—that is, Ibn Uqbah—narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban narrated to me, from Ibn Muhayriz, from Abu Said al-Khudri: During the expedition to Banu al-Mustaliq, they captured female prisoners and wanted to have relations with them without making them pregnant. They asked the Prophet about withdrawal. He said: “It is not necessary for you not to do that, for Allah has already written every soul He will create until the Day of Resurrection.” Mujahid reported from Qazah: I heard Abu Said say that the Prophet said: “There is no created soul except that Allah is its Creator.”

Muadh ibn Fadalah narrated to me; Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas: The Prophet said: “Allah will gather the believers on the Day of Resurrection, and they will say, ‘If only we could seek an intercessor with our Lord so He would relieve us from this place.’ They will go to Adam and say, ‘Adam, do you not see that Allah created you with His Hand, made His angels prostrate to you, and taught you the names of everything? Intercede for us with your Lord so He will relieve us from this place.’ He will say, ‘I am not the one for this,’ and mention the sin he committed. ‘Go to Noah, for he was the first messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth.’ They will go to Noah, and he will say, ‘I am not the one for this,’ and mention the sin he committed. ‘Go to Abraham, the beloved of the Most Merciful.’ They will go to Abraham, and he will say, ‘I am not the one for this,’ and mention his errors. ‘Go to Moses, a servant to whom Allah gave the Torah and spoke directly.’ They will go to Moses, and he will say, ‘I am not the one for this,’ and mention the sin he committed. ‘Go to Jesus, Allah’s servant and Messenger, His word and spirit.’ They will go to Jesus, and he will say, ‘I am not the one for this. Go to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, a servant whose past and future sins have been forgiven.’ They will come to me, and I will go and ask my Lord for permission. Permission will be given to me. When I see my Lord, I will fall down in prostration before Him, and He will leave me as long as He wishes. Then it will be said to me, ‘Raise your head, Muhammad. Speak and you will be heard; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.’ I will praise my Lord with praises He has taught me, then intercede. He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return; when I see my Lord, I will fall down in prostration, and He will leave me as long as He wishes. Then it will be said, ‘Raise your head, Muhammad. Speak and you will be heard; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.’ I will praise my Lord with praises He has taught me, then intercede. He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return; when I see my Lord, I will fall down in prostration, and He will leave me as long as He wishes. Then it will be said, ‘Raise your head, Muhammad. Speak and you will be heard; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.’ I will praise my Lord with praises He has taught me, then intercede. He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return and say, ‘My Lord, no one remains in the Fire except those whom the Quran has confined there and for whom eternal residence has become due.’” The Prophet said: “Everyone who said, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ and had good in his heart weighing a barley grain will come out of the Fire. Then everyone who said, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ and had good in his heart weighing a wheat grain will come out of the Fire. Then everyone who said, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ and had good in his heart weighing an atom will come out of the Fire.”

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuaib informed us; Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Allah’s Hand is full; spending does not diminish it. He gives abundantly by night and by day. Do you see what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? It has not diminished what is in His Hand.” He said: “His Throne was over the water, and in His other Hand is the balance; He lowers and raises.”

Muqaddam ibn Muhammad narrated to us; he said: My uncle al-Qasim ibn Yahya narrated to me, from Ubaydullah, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: “On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will grasp the earth, and the heavens will be in His right hand. Then He will say, ‘I am the King.’” Said reported it from Malik. Umar ibn Hamzah said: I heard Salim say: I heard Ibn Umar report this from the Prophet. Abu al-Yaman said: Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri; Abu Salamah informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah said, “Allah will grasp the earth.”

Musaddad narrated to us; he heard Yahya ibn Said, from Sufyan. Mansur and Sulayman narrated to me, from Ibrahim, from Abidah, from Abdullah: A Jewish man came to the Prophet and said, “Muhammad, Allah holds the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the mountains on one finger, the trees on one finger, and all creatures on one finger. Then He says, ‘I am the King.’” The Messenger of Allah laughed until his molar teeth showed, then recited: “They did not appraise Allah with the appraisal due to Him” (6:91). Yahya ibn Said said: Fudayl ibn Iyad added, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Abidah, from Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah laughed in amazement and affirmation of what the man said.

Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us. I heard Ibrahim say: I heard Alqamah say that Abdullah said: A man from the People of the Book came to the Prophet and said, “Abu al-Qasim, Allah holds the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the trees and soil on one finger, and all creatures on one finger. Then He says, ‘I am the King, I am the King.’” I saw the Prophet laugh until his molar teeth showed, then recite: “They did not appraise Allah with the appraisal due to Him” (6:91).

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us; Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from Warrad, the scribe of al-Mughirah, from al-Mughirah, who said: Sad ibn Ubadah said, “If I saw a man with my wife, I would strike him with the sharp side of the sword.” This reached the Messenger of Allah, who said: “Are you amazed at Sad’s protective jealousy? By Allah, I am more protective than he is, and Allah is more protective than I am. Because of Allah’s protective jealousy, He has forbidden immoral acts, both public and private. No one loves that an excuse be accepted more than Allah, and for that reason He sent the bringers of glad tidings and the warners. No one loves praise more than Allah, and for that reason Allah promised Paradise.” Ubaydullah ibn Amr reported from Abd al-Malik the wording, “No one is more protective than Allah.”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Malik informed us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sad, who said: The Prophet said to a man, “Do you have anything of the Quran with you?” He said, “Yes, this chapter and that chapter,” naming some chapters.

Abdan narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Amash, from Jami ibn Shaddad, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, from Imran ibn Husayn, who said: I was with the Prophet when some people from Banu Tamim came to him. He said: “Accept the glad tidings, Banu Tamim.” They said, “You have given us glad tidings, so give us something.” Some people from Yemen then entered, and he said: “Accept the glad tidings, people of Yemen, since Banu Tamim did not accept them.” They said, “We accept them. We have come to gain understanding of the religion and ask you about how this matter began.” He said: “Allah existed, and there was nothing before Him. His Throne was over the water. Then He created the heavens and the earth and wrote everything in the Record.” Then a man came to me and said, “Imran, go find your she-camel; it has gone off.” I went to look for it, and the mirage stretched out beyond it. By Allah, I wished it had gone and that I had not stood up.

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Mamar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “Indeed, Allah’s right hand is full; spending does not diminish it. He gives abundantly by night and day. Consider what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth: what is in His right hand has not decreased. His Throne is over the water, and in His other hand is abundance—or withholding—and He raises and lowers.”

Ahmad narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: Zayd ibn Harithah came complaining, and the Prophet kept saying: “Fear Allah and keep your wife.” Aishah said: If the Messenger of Allah had concealed anything, he would have concealed this. Zaynab used to boast to the Prophet’s wives, saying: “Your families married you off, but Allah married me from above the seven heavens.” Thabit reported that the verse, “You concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose, and you feared the people” (33:37), was revealed concerning Zaynab and Zayd ibn Harithah.

Khallad ibn Yahya narrated to us; Isa ibn Tahman narrated to us, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The verse of the veil was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh. On that day, he served bread and meat at her wedding feast. She used to boast to the wives of the Prophet, saying: “Allah married me in Heaven.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuaib informed us; Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “When Allah had decreed creation, He wrote with Him above His Throne: ‘My mercy preceded My anger.’”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Fulayh narrated to me; my father narrated to me; Hilal narrated to me, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “Whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger, establishes prayer, and fasts Ramadan has a right upon Allah that He admit him to Paradise, whether he emigrates in the path of Allah or stays in the land where he was born.” They said, “Messenger of Allah, shall we not inform the people of this?” He said: “In Paradise are one hundred levels that Allah has prepared for those who strive in His path. The distance between each two levels is like the distance between heaven and earth. When you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the best and highest part of Paradise. Above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow.”

Yahya ibn Jafar narrated to us; Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Ibrahim—the Taymi—from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque while the Messenger of Allah was sitting there. When the sun set, he said: “Abu Dharr, do you know where it goes?” I said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “It goes and seeks permission to prostrate, and permission is granted to it. It is as though it is told, ‘Return from where you came,’ and then it rises from its setting place.” Then he recited, according to Abdullah’s recitation: “That is its appointed course.”

Musa narrated to us, from Ibrahim. Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from Ubayd ibn al-Sabbaq, that Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to him. Al-Layth said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Sabbaq, that Zayd ibn Thabit told him: Abu Bakr sent for me, so I searched for the Quran until I found the end of Surat al-Tawbah with Abu Khuzaymah al-Ansari. I found it with no one else: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves...” through the end of Surat Bara’ah (9:128). Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Yunus, with the same report, and he said, “with Abu Khuzaymah al-Ansari.”

Muala ibn Asad narrated to us; Wuhayb narrated to us, from Said, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: During distress, the Prophet used to say: “There is no god but Allah, the All-Knowing, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Noble Throne.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Yahya, from his father, from Abu Said al-Khudri, from the Prophet, who said: “People will be struck unconscious on the Day of Resurrection. I will be the first to recover, and Moses will be holding one of the supports of the Throne.” Al-Majishun reported from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “I will be the first to be raised, and Moses will be holding the Throne.”

Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Angels alternate among you by night and by day, and they meet at the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend. He asks them, though He knows best about you, ‘How did you leave My servants?’ They say, ‘We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.’”

Khalid ibn Makhlad said: Sulayman narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever gives charity equal to a date from lawful earnings—and nothing ascends to Allah except what is good—Allah accepts it with His right hand, then nurtures it for its giver just as one of you raises a young horse, until it becomes like a mountain.” Waraqah reported from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Said ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with the wording: “Nothing ascends to Allah except what is good.”

Abd al-Ala ibn Hammad narrated to us; Yazid ibn Zuray narrated to us; Said narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ibn Abbas: When the Prophet was distressed, he used to supplicate: “There is no god but Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the Noble Throne.”

Qabisah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nuaim—or Abu Nuaim, Qabisah was uncertain—from Abu Said, who said: A small piece of gold was sent to the Prophet, and he divided it among four people. Ishaq ibn Nasr narrated to me; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Sufyan informed us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nuaim, from Abu Said al-Khudri, who said: Ali, while in Yemen, sent a small piece of gold in its ore to the Prophet. He divided it among al-Aqra ibn Habis al-Hanzali, one of Banu Mujashi; Uyaynah ibn Badr al-Fazari; Alqamah ibn Ulathah al-Amiri, one of Banu Kilab; and Zayd al-Khayl al-Ta’i, one of Banu Nabhan. Quraysh and the Ansar became angry and said, “He gives to the chiefs of Najd and leaves us?” He said: “I am only trying to draw them close.” A man with sunken eyes, a prominent forehead, a thick beard, and shaved head came forward and said, “Muhammad, fear Allah.” The Prophet said: “Who would obey Allah if I disobeyed Him? Would He entrust me with the people of the earth while you do not?” A man among the people asked permission to kill him—I think it was Khalid ibn al-Walid—but the Prophet stopped him. When the man turned away, the Prophet said: “From this man’s descendants will come a people who recite the Quran, but it will not pass beyond their throats. They will leave Islam as an arrow passes through its target. They will kill the Muslims and leave the idolaters. If I live to see them, I will kill them as the people of Ad were killed.”

Ayyash ibn al-Walid narrated to us; Waki narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: I asked the Prophet about Allah’s words, “The sun runs to its appointed course” (36:38). He said: “Its appointed course is beneath the Throne.”

Amr ibn Awn narrated to us; Khalid and Hushaym narrated to us, from Ismail, from Qays, from Jarir, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet when he looked at the full moon and said: “You will see your Lord as you see this moon, without crowding or difficulty in seeing Him. If you are able not to be overcome with regard to a prayer before sunrise and a prayer before sunset, then do so.”

Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us; Asim ibn Yusuf al-Yarbu’i narrated to us; Abu Shihab narrated to us, from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Prophet said: “You will see your Lord with your own eyes.”

Abdah ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Husayn al-Jufi narrated to us, from Zaidah; Bayan ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim. Jarir narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah came out to us on the night of the full moon and said: “You will see your Lord on the Day of Resurrection as you see this moon, without crowding or difficulty in seeing Him.”
